definitions.explanation: Daikon radish grated into a fine, juicy pulp. A staple condiment in Japanese cuisine, served alongside grilled fish, tempura, noodles, and many other dishes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{焼|や}き{魚|ざかな}→焼き魚：13406_yakizakana⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{大根|だいこん}おろし⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{添|そ}える→添える：13315_soeru⟧。
examples.english: Serve grated daikon alongside grilled fish.

examples.japanese: ⟦{天|てん}ぷら→天ぷら：04948_tenpura⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{大根|だいこん}おろし⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れた→入れる：01098_ireru⟧つゆ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{合|あ}う→合う：10466_au⟧。
examples.english: Dipping sauce with grated daikon goes well with tempura.

examples.japanese: {大根|だいこん}おろし⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{消化|しょうか}→消化：04200_shouka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{助|たす}ける→助ける：00895_tasukeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{脂|あぶら}っこい→脂っこい：14728_aburakkoi⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{添|そ}える→添える：13315_soeru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Grated daikon is said to aid digestion, so it is often served alongside greasy dishes.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{大根|だいこん}→大根：05186_daikon⟧ (daikon radish) and おろし (grated, from ⟦{下|お}ろす→下ろす：02029_orosu⟧ meaning to grate). One of the most essential condiments in Japanese cuisine.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大根|だいこん}おろし⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{添|そ}える→添える：13315_soeru⟧: to serve grated daikon as a garnish
- {大根|だいこん}おろし⟦アート→アート：10713_aato⟧: decorative shapes made from grated daikon
- おろし⟦ポン{酢|ず}→ポン酢：11115_ponzu⟧: grated daikon with ponzu sauce
- おろし⟦{蕎麦|そば}→蕎麦：14329_soba⟧: soba noodles topped with grated daikon

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦おろし{金|がね}→おろし金：07038_oroshigane⟧: grater (the tool used to grate daikon)
- ⟦{薬味|やくみ}→薬味：04964_yakumi⟧: condiment, garnish — the broader category that includes grated daikon
- もみじおろし: grated daikon mixed with chili pepper, creating a red-tinged condiment

CULTURAL NOTE:
{大根|だいこん}おろし is believed to contain digestive enzymes that help break down fats, which is why it traditionally accompanies ⟦{天|てん}ぷら→天ぷら：04948_tenpura⟧, ⟦{焼|や}き{魚|ざかな}→焼き魚：13406_yakizakana⟧, and other rich dishes. The tip of the daikon produces spicier おろし, while the top portion closer to the leaves is milder and sweeter.
